gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 is the only ~2 kWh pick that can be doubled for a longer outage: Anker's BP2000 Expansion Battery (Gen 2) is 'exclusively designed for' it and takes it to 4,096 Wh, and Anker says that battery is 'Not compatible with Anker SOLIX F2000'. The BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 takes no expansion battery at all.
standout_why: Compared against The Outage Brief (cited), Home Power Facts (cited), WattPowerStation (cited) and our own page. The Outage Brief says the Elite 200 V2 'isn't expandable' and covers expansion only for the DELTA Pro 3 and F3800. It names the C2000 Gen 2 only in a table and gives no battery model, ceiling or exclusion for it. WattPowerStation gives only a pooled UPS range ('10 to 20 milliseconds') with no figure per model and says nothing about expansion batteries. Home Power Facts covers neither UPS nor expansion. The Yahoo/CNET page returned 403 and could not be checked.
decides: It confirms the C2000 Gen 2 over the Elite 200 V2 for a shopper who isn't sure 2 kWh will last 24 hours. Both are about 2 kWh, but only the C2000 Gen 2 can grow to 4,096 Wh with one Anker-specified battery. It also has a maker-stated 10 ms UPS and a TT-30R outlet. StorageReview lists the Elite 200 V2's UPS at 15 ms. The Elite 200 V2 stays the cheaper fixed-capacity choice at $899 on bluettipower.com today. The BLUETTI AC200L can take the B300K (2,764.8 Wh), but The Outage Brief marks the AC200L discontinued.

findings.label: Compatible expansion battery
findings.value: B300K, 2,764.8 Wh; BLUETTI says it 'seamlessly integrates with AC200L, AC200MAX, AC300, Apex 300 and AC500'; $1,099 (was $1,199)
